_README: Price table for the Budget Guard's pre-call estimates.
Entries with "last_verified": null are UNVERIFIED — the router REFUSES to make a
live (billable) call using one. Look the real price up in the provider's pricing
page/dashboard, put it in, and set last_verified to today (YYYY-MM-DD).
units: 'per_call' = flat USD per request. 'per_second' = USD x output duration.
Optional per-rate fields:
supports: [...]        -> the model's ACCEPTED input field names. The adapter sends
nothing outside this list, so an unsupported parameter is
never smuggled into a request.
usd_by / price_by     -> price varies by an input param (e.g. resolution tier).
price_expires         -> promo end date; the rate reads as UNVERIFIED from then.
params: {stage: {...}} -> per-stage input values ('all' applies to every stage).
identity_via_image     -> the model carries persona identity through image_url, so a
persona job must supply a reference still.
fixed_durations: [..]  -> model only emits these lengths; requests snap UP and are
billed at the tier. Omit for models billing by the second.
routing stages:
draft / final          -> the two video stages of the draft-then-approve gate.
still                  -> a NEW image from text alone: a face for a new influencer,
or a product/ad still. Cannot preserve an existing face.
still_identity         -> a new image OF AN EXISTING persona, seeded from their
locked reference. 10x the price of text-to-image, and the
only one of the two that keeps the face.

fal:minimax/h3-max/image-to-video.source: fal.ai/models/minimax/h3-max/image-to-video — schema and price read from the model page
fal:minimax/h3-max/image-to-video.price_note: promo launch rate, 50% off; reverts 2026-09-01 to 480P $0.05/s, 768P $0.08/s

runware:DRAFT_IMAGE_MODEL.source: TODO: verify at runware.ai — cheap still for a framing check

runware:DRAFT_VIDEO_MODEL.source: TODO: verify at runware.ai — cheap i2v for a motion check

fal:fal-ai/flux/schnell.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/flux/schnell - '$0.003 per megapixel', billed rounded UP to the nearest megapixel. Our 720x1280 default is 0.92 MP -> 1 MP -> $0.003. Change image_size and this estimate is wrong.
fal:fal-ai/flux/schnell.price_note: text-to-image: creates a NEW face. It cannot reproduce an existing persona - use still_identity for that.

fal:fal-ai/flux/dev/image-to-image.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/flux/dev/image-to-image - '$0.03 per megapixel', billed rounded UP. Output size follows the INPUT image, so a large reference still costs proportionally more than this 1 MP estimate.
fal:fal-ai/flux/dev/image-to-image.price_note: 10x the text-to-image price, and still ~1/10th of a video render. This is the one that keeps an influencer's face.

fal:fal-ai/wan-25-preview/image-to-video.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/wan-25-preview/image-to-video - '$0.05 per second for 480p, $0.10 per second for 720p, $0.15 per second for 1080p'. Schema from the endpoint's OpenAPI: duration is the STRING enum 5|10.
fal:fal-ai/wan-25-preview/image-to-video.price_note: The versatile one: image-to-video that ALSO takes an optional audio_url (3-30s), so it covers both ordinary clips and the Fish Audio lipsync pipeline without a second model. Only emits 5s or 10s.

fal:fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/im.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/image-to-video - 'For 5s video your request will cost $0.35. For every additional second you will be charged $0.07.' Schema from the endpoint's OpenAPI.
fal:fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/im.price_note: Volume workhorse. No resolution parameter, so there is no cheap draft tier - a 5s draft costs the same $0.35 as 5s of the final.

fal:fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/ima.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video - fal quotes 'Each 1080p 5 second video costs roughly $0.62', i.e. $0.124/s AT 1080p. Other resolutions are priced by video tokens ((h*w*fps*dur)/1024 at $2.5/M) which this table cannot express - so the 480p draft estimate is WRONG and cost drift will flag it. Verify before routing drafts here.
fal:fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/ima.price_note: Premium quality, but the only entry whose price our estimator cannot model faithfully across resolutions.

fal:fal-ai/veo3.1/image-to-video.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/veo3.1/image-to-video - '$0.20 per second at 720p/1080p without audio, $0.40 with audio; 4K $0.40 without / $0.60 with'. Schema from the endpoint's OpenAPI: duration is the STRING enum 4s|6s|8s.
fal:fal-ai/veo3.1/image-to-video.price_note: Highest quality, highest price. generate_audio is forced FALSE here - native audio would give a different voice on every clip.

fal:fal-ai/bytedance/omnihuman.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/bytedance/omnihuman - '$0.14 per second' of output. Inputs are image_url + audio_url only; max audio 30s.
fal:fal-ai/bytedance/omnihuman.price_note: Audio-driven avatar: reference plate + a Fish Audio track in, lipsynced clip out. Takes NO prompt, so framing and action come entirely from the plate. 30s cap covers most UGC ads in a single clip.

fal:fal-ai/qwen-image.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/qwen-image - 'Your request will cost $0.02 per megapixel. Images are billed by rounding up to the nearest megapixel.' 720x1280 = 0.92 MP -> 1 MP -> $0.02.
fal:fal-ai/qwen-image.price_note: Mid-tier text-to-image. Notably stronger than flux/schnell at rendering legible text, which matters for product packaging.

fal:fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/text-to.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/text-to-image - 'Your request will cost $0.03 per image.' Billed per IMAGE, not per megapixel, so size does not change the price.
fal:fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/text-to.price_note: Flat per-image pricing - the only text-to-image entry whose estimate stays correct if you change image_size.

fal:fal-ai/nano-banana/edit.source: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/nano-banana/edit - 'Your request will cost $0.039 per image.' Takes image_urls as an ARRAY, not a single image_url.
fal:fal-ai/nano-banana/edit.price_note: Identity-preserving editing. Because it conditions on a LIST of images it is the natural fit for a reference pack - several plates at once rather than one.

anthropic:claude-opus-5.source: Anthropic API pricing: Claude Opus 5 $5.00/1M input, $25.00/1M output. The $0.012 flat figure is the RESERVATION estimate for a typical UGC script (~500 in / ~400 out); every call settles at its exact measured token cost, so drift here is informational, not a mispriced cap.
anthropic:claude-opus-5.price_note: Roughly 1% of the video it writes. Cheap enough that the reason to meter it is the invariant — every paid call gets a ledger row — not the money.
